findings.proposition: Order D.I. 590 states that at the close of Qorvo's case the Akoustis defendants made two oral Rule 50(a) motions; the court denied the first, a Daubert/Rule 702 challenge to Qorvo's trade secret damages experts, and reserved ruling on the second, on UDTPA actual injury.
findings.target: Qorvo v. Akoustis - Akoustis Rule 50(a) motions at close of Qorvo's case

spans.quote: At the close of Pla intiff’s case, Defendants ’ made two oral Motions pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 50(a). The Court denied the first motion, which related to a Daubert/Fed. R. Civ. P. 702 challenge to Plaintiffs ’ Trade Secret Damages Experts, but reserved ruling on the second.
Defendants’ 50(a) motion argued that there is insufficient evidence to support a finding of actual injury to Plaintiff under the North Carolina Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

findings.proposition: In D.I. 590 the court found that Qorvo bases its damages exclusively on the DTSA head-start benefit damages provision, that its sole damages expert opines North Carolina damages would equal the DTSA amount, that Qorvo provided no evidence it lost market share or profit because of the alleged misappropriation, and that there is no record evidence the parties compete in the same geographic area for the same customers.
findings.target: Qorvo v. Akoustis - court's view of Qorvo's damages evidence (head start) and actual loss record

spans.quote: Plaintiffs base their damages assessment exclusively on the DT SA’s head start benefit damages provision. Plaintiffs’ sole damages expert does not reference North Carolina law in her report, and only opines that the damages under North Carolina law would be in the same amount as those calculated under the DTSA.

Plaintiff has not provided any evidence that they lost market share or suffered lost profit because of Defendants’ alleged misappropriation. Indeed, while there is testimony that the Parties are competitors, there is no evidence in the record that they compete in the same geographic area, for the same customers at each others’ expense.

findings.proposition: D.I. 590 states that head-start damages calculate the benefit to the defendant of having certain profits (in this case, revenues) earlier, that there is no record evidence those revenues would otherwise have gone to Qorvo, and that head-start benefits are not a proxy for damage to Qorvo under the UDTPA.
findings.target: Qorvo v. Akoustis - head-start damages method based on Akoustis revenues

spans.quote: Head start damages calculate the benefit to Defendant from having certain profits (or, in this case, revenues) earlier than they would have. But there is no evidence in the record that those revenues otherwise would have gone t o Plaintiffs, or that they resulted in any expansion of market share at Plaintiffs’ expense. findings.proposition: Akoustis's 8-K of 27 October 2023 reports that on October 24, 2023 Nasdaq notified it that its closing bid price had been below $1.00 for 30 consecutive trading days, so it no longer complied with the Nasdaq Capital Market $1.00 minimum bid price requirement (Rule 5550(a)(2)), and that it had until April 22, 2024 to regain compliance by a closing bid of at least $1.00 for 10 consecutive trading days, with a possible additional 180-day period.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. - Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency notice (October 2023)

spans.quote: On October 24, 2023, Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”) received a written notice (the “Notice”) from the Listing Qualifications Department of Nasdaq Stock Market (“Nasdaq”) indicating that, because the closing bid price for the Company’s common stock has fallen below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive trading days, the Company was no longer in compliance with the $1.00 Minimum Bid Price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2)
To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company’s common stock must meet or exceed $1.00 per share for a minimum of 10 consecutive trading days prior to April 22, 2024.
If the Company meets these requirements, the Nasdaq staff would be expected to grant an additional 180 calendar days for the Company to regain compliance with Bid Price Requirement.

findings.proposition: Akoustis's 10-Q (Nasdaq notification note) states that, not having regained compliance by April 22, 2024, the Company requested and was granted an additional 180 calendar days, expiring October 21, 2024, to regain compliance with the $1.00 bid price requirement, and that it will consider available options which could include seeking to effect a reverse stock split.

findings.proposition: In D.I. 590 the court states that North Carolina courts have upheld UDTPA liability findings with only nominal damages; that UDTPA damage categories are more limited than under the DTSA; and that North Carolina courts allow disgorgement of defendants' profits as damages where it proxies the plaintiff's injury but have not recognized a defendant's head-start benefits as such a proxy.
findings.target: Qorvo v. Akoustis - D.I. 590 reasoning on categories of UDTPA damages

spans.quote: Carolina courts have upheld liability findings even where juries have awarded only nominal damages.
The categories of damages cognizable under the UDTPA, however, are more limited than those cognizable under the federal Defend Trade Secrets Act.

North Carolina Courts have allowed for disgorgement of profits by defendants to serve as damages where they are proxies for injury by plaintiff, but has not recognized head start benefits to the Defendants as such a proxy.

spans.quote: Qorvo identified a subset of those trade secrets—104 trade secrets—to present to the jury (the “Asserted Trade Secrets”). The Asserted Trade Secrets can be organized into ten groups:

Trade Secret Group 3: Qorvo’s trimming methods and procedures; Trade Secret Group 4: Qorvo’s evaluation board design rules and schematics; Trade Secret Group 5: Qorvo’s product development process and testing procedures;
Trade Secret Group 6: Qorvo’s systems, processes, and procedures for testing reliability and mean-time-to-failure of parts;
Trade Secret Group 7: Qorvo manufacturing, assembly, and change procedures;

Trade Secret Group 8: Qorvo product roadmaps and product prototypes; Trade Secret Group 9: trade secrets relating to job structures and employee compensation; and Trade Secret Group 10: Qorvo’s tax and corporate compliance structure and know-how.

provenance.derivation: Qorvo's requested non-duplicative compensatory figures in its statement of intended proof, summed: $66.1M head-start unjust enrichment (fnd_017) + $1,146,604 corrective advertising (fnd_024) + $279,808 patent royalty (fnd_019) = $67,526,412, before any exemplary, treble, fees, interest or costs.
